items.title: PDL-BWR-26-001, Charles Street Terminal Update
notes:
Rod Regier, Commissioner of Planning, Development, and Legislative Services, provided an introduction to the report.

Matthew Chandy, Director of Build Waterloo Region, provided a presentation that outlined the history of the subject site and what Regional staff have done so far which includes beginning an environmental assessment and public engagement strategy. Staff are seeking direction to proceed with the re-development in a phased manner in order to better respond to market conditions.

In response to questions from Committee M. Chandy confirmed the next steps in the project pipeline and when procurement would begin.

Staff confirmed that the next step would be to incorporate the priorities of both Council and the public and move forward with those priorities as the guiding principles. 

In response to concerns from Committee, R. Regier explained that staff can report back on the potential impacts of different ownership models for this site.

items.title: PDL-GDS-26-004, Update on the Implementation of the Corporate Climate Action Plan
notes:
R. Regier provided an introduction to the report.

Meaghan Eastwood, Manager, Climate and Sustainability and Max Chute, Corporate Energy Analyst, provided a presentation on the corporate climate action plan as well as recommended construction standards to meet LEED certification. 

In response to questions from Committee, staff elaborated on the various strategies that staff are looking at to both reduce corporate emissions as well as emissions from the public.

Staff also confirmed that the largest source of corporate transmissions is from GRT although GRT transmissions reduce community emissions making it an overall net benefit, regional buildings are the next largest source of corporate emissions.

items.title: PDL-GDS-26-006, Regional Forest Management Program Update
notes:
R. Regier provided an introduction to the report.

Andrew Puchalski, Regional Forester, provided a presentation on highlights from 2025, what work has been done so far for 2026, and upcoming projects and priorities with regional forests. 

In response to questions from Committee, A. Puchalski confirmed that the regional forest network is currently open to the public, staff have worked to substantially update its web pages for pubic information.

Staff also confirmed that while they do have good relationships with area municipalities they primarily work on regional forest management.

Staff also confirmed that if Council expressed interest in it, staff would be supportive of expanding the regional forest network.

motions.item_title: PDL-GDS-26-007, Tax Increment Grant – 161 Ottawa Street South
motions.text: That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following actions regarding the property municipally known as 161 Ottawa Street South in the City of Kitchener, as described in Report PDL-GDS-26-007, dated March 10, 2026: Approve a joint Tax Increment Grant with the Regional amount not to exceed $114,580, to be financed from the incremental tax revenue for the property following remediation, redevelopment and reassessment; and Authorize the Region’s Commissioner of Planning, Development and Legislative Services and Commissioner, Corporate Services / Chief Financial Officer to execute any associated agreements, assignments, amendments or other related documents with the registered owner of 161 Ottawa Street South in the City of Kitchener, with the form and content of such Tax Increment Grant agreement(s), any subsequent assignments of the agreement, or other related documents to be satisfactory to the Regional Solicitor.
motions.text_html:
That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following actions regarding the property municipally known as 161 Ottawa Street South in the City of Kitchener, as described in Report PDL-GDS-26-007, dated March 10, 2026:

  1. Approve a joint Tax Increment Grant with the Regional amount not to exceed $114,580, to be financed from the incremental tax revenue for the property following remediation, redevelopment and reassessment; and
  2. Authorize the Region’s Commissioner of Planning, Development and Legislative Services and Commissioner, Corporate Services / Chief Financial Officer to execute any associated agreements, assignments, amendments or other related documents with the registered owner of 161 Ottawa Street South in the City of Kitchener, with the form and content of such Tax Increment Grant agreement(s), any subsequent assignments of the agreement, or other related documents to be satisfactory to the Regional Solicitor.

motions.item_title: TSD-TRP-26-003, Regional Road Assumption Criteria - Policy Update
motions.text: That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo adopt the revised and updated Regional Road Assumption Criteria Policy as outlined in report TSD-TRP-26-003 dated March 10, 2026.
motions.text_html: That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo adopt the revised and updated Regional Road Assumption Criteria Policy as outlined in report TSD-TRP-26-003 dated March 10, 2026.

motions.text: That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo proceed with the multi-phased plan for developing Charles Street Terminal, as outlined in report PDL-BWR-26-001 dated March 10, 2026. And that Regional staff report to the Sustainability, Infrastructure, and Development Committee as part of a subsequent Report regarding the Charles Street Terminal procurement framework on: Options to retain public land ownership of all or portions of the site, and; A specific affordable and/or non-market housing framework for re-development across the site, consistent with Building Better Futures.
motions.text_html:
That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo proceed with the multi-phased plan for developing Charles Street Terminal, as outlined in report PDL-BWR-26-001 dated March 10, 2026.

And that Regional staff report to the Sustainability, Infrastructure, and Development Committee as part of a subsequent Report regarding the Charles Street Terminal procurement framework on:

  • Options to retain public land ownership of all or portions of the site, and;
  • A specific affordable and/or non-market housing framework for re-development across the site, consistent with Building Better Futures.

motions.item_title: EES-FFM-26-001, Minimum Sustainable Construction Standard for Regional Facilities
motions.text: That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo approves targeting the Canada Green Building Council’s Zero Carbon Building – Design (ZCB-Design) standard for new Regional facilities, replacing the existing LEED™ Silver standard, subject to project-specific feasibility and approved capital budgets as set out in report dated March 10, 2026.
motions.text_html: That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo approves targeting the Canada Green Building Council’s Zero Carbon Building – Design (ZCB-Design) standard for new Regional facilities, replacing the existing LEED™ Silver standard, subject to project-specific feasibility and approved capital budgets as set out in report dated March 10, 2026.
